Why a Kashmiri Cattle Rearer Still Depends on a Lake That Made Her Sick

Anchar Lake in Srinagar, Kashmir, has shrunk drastically since the 1890s due to encroachment and untreated sewage, causing thousands of waterborne illness cases among dependent residents.

Even with piped water at home, severe systemic infrastructure gaps and economic desperation force residents back into contact with toxic waters.

The crisis persists because institutional power protects short-term development over community survival, shifting environmental burdens onto marginalized workers who lack safe alternatives.
